name: Brock Bowers

background.fact: Born December 13, 2002 in Napa, California; attended Napa High School, where he played football and basketball, and as a junior set a school record with 14 touchdown receptions.
His senior high school season was canceled by COVID-19 restrictions in California, yet he was still named to the All-American Bowl.
He played at Georgia, where he was a three-time All-American, two-time John Mackey Award winner, and won two national championships.
The Raiders drafted him in the first round (13th overall) in 2024; as a rookie he set records for receptions in a season and most receiving yards by a tight end, with Pro Bowl and All-Pro honors.

family.fact: His parents met at Utah State University: his mother was an All-American softball player later inducted into the school's athletic Hall of Fame and then a high school math teacher and softball coach; his father played center for the Utah State football team and later founded a construction company.
He has a sister who plays softball at Sacramento State. Nothing further about family (partner, children) was found in public reporting: not found.

scouts_read: Bowers is healthy and should play, so the question is volume with a first-time starter. He has been the Raiders' top target all year (22 percent of targets) and has reached 70 yards in all seven games, which gives him a safe floor even with a quarterback change. The game script is the risk: Las Vegas is a 6.5 point underdog with an implied total of about 17, in a dome against a Seattle team that has covered tight ends well. A rookie under pressure often leans on the nearest big target, which supports a heavy target count of 8 or more. I would project a steady game of roughly 12 to 17 points, with touchdown luck deciding whether it goes higher.
